_comment: CALIBRATION 2026-10-31 (see PROTOCOL.md): control arm only, N=3, on the private Attica corpus task attica-a2; the seed is off-tree and its digest is in the protocol. atomaRuns is 0 on purpose.

primary.goal: The Attica control page becomes unusable once a collection history is retained: with about a thousand saved listings and a dozen schedule history entries, every one-second poll of GET /api/status returns the complete store, raw listing payloads (extra_json) and the full rows of every history entry included, several megabytes per poll, and overlapping polls and recovery retries multiply the reads. Fix this in the browser/ control server and client (browser/control-server.ts, browser/control-connection.ts, browser/control.ts and any new module you need) without changing stored data. (1) GET /api/status must answer under 500 KB with 1,010 complete listings and 12 history entries: each row keeps its presentation fields (identifiant, url, prix, localisation, description and the like) and omits raw payload fields such as extra_json; a history entry carries its time, status, reason, error, current page and its row COUNT, never the rows themselves. (2) GET /api/schedule must answer under 10 KB in that same state, and POST /api/schedule returns the same reduced shape. (3) GET /api/listings and the exports under /api/exports/ keep returning the complete records byte-for-byte, and polling must never rewrite attica-listings.json, attica-state.json, attica-schedule.json, the checkpoint or the exports. (4) createControlConnection in browser/control-connection.ts gains a poll() method beside refresh(): poll() returns the pending request's promise when one is in flight instead of starting another, refresh() always starts a fresh request (a manual refresh after an action is never served by a stale pending poll), a scheduled recovery retry is superseded by the next poll rather than doubling the reads, and invalidate() keeps its meaning. The control page's periodic timer uses poll() and its manual refresh uses refresh(). Keep the existing behaviour of every other route and of the UI, keep strict TypeScript, add maintained tests for the status size, the preserved complete endpoints and the connection semantics, and run npm run check and npm run build. No dependency upgrades and no real xe.gr/Spitogatos traffic.
